title: Predictive Alerting for Hypoglycemia in 812 Bytes: A TinyML Approach for Wearable Platforms
content: Predictive hypoglycemia alerts are a critical safety feature of wearable glucose monitors. The design of such systems is impeded by a lack of comparative data on algorithmic cost, clinical effectiveness, and hardware performance. This work addresses this gap by developing a resource-efficient predictive alerting system based on 30-minute glucose forecasting. The system employs a 737-parameter feed-forward network, evaluated against eleven predictors across three memory orders, subjected to fixed-point quantization, and deployed on five Cortex-M microcontrollers. The proposed model attains 19.22 mg/dL, trailing a 61 kB reference by only 0.111 mg/dL on 34 held-out patients, and occupies 812 bytes as an 8-bit integer graph with 284 bytes of working memory. Cycle counts across the five platforms range from 5,807 to 8,914, exhibiting a 1.54× spread that reverses latency-based ordering.Two findings reshape the value of model compression. Inference consumes less than 1% of average power at a five-minute duty cycle, rendering per-inference energy an inadequate metric. The determining factor is whether the 72-byte state fits in backup registers, enabling Standby sleep and superseding microcontroller selection by a factor of four to six. Managing sensor dropout rather than discarding affected windows elevates severe-episode detection from 76.9% to 86.7% and twenty-minute warning from 75.1% to 85.0%, at 2.93 false alarms per patient-day across 2,764 episodes from 34 held-out patients. A linear ceiling at 19.65 mg/dL and an unreproducible benchmark baseline are also documented.
